report.source_text: The patient was started with a high-protein diet. Long-chain triglycerides were replaced with medium-chain triglycerides. He was regularly followed up in the hospital. On reassessments, there was a gradual improvement in his symptoms.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 6-year-old boy presented with recurrent diarrhea, weight loss, bilateral lower limb edema, hypoalbuminemia, and lymphopenia. Early workup with abdominal CECT showed jejunal thickening, echogenic fat islands in mesentery, and enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes with minimal pelvic ascites. Subsequent duodenal biopsy revealed villous blunting and dilated lymphatic channels filled with proteinaceous fluid and lymphoplasmacytic infiltration consistent with duodenal lymphangiectasia. The patient was treated with a high-protein, medium-chain triglyceride diet and showed gradual symptomatic improvement on follow-up.
